annotation.title_clean: Principes pour des technologies de l'intelligence artificielle (IA) générative responsables, dignes de confiance et respectueuses de la vie privée
annotation.title_en: Principles for responsible, trustworthy and privacy-protective generative AI technologies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Commissariat à la protection de la vie privée du Canada (with provincial and territorial privacy commissioners)
annotation.venue: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada website
annotation.summary_en: Joint guidance from Canada's federal, provincial and territorial privacy commissioners applying nine key privacy principles to generative AI for developers, providers and user organisations. It stresses that existing privacy law applies, and addresses vulnerable groups, prohibited uses, transparency, accountability, accuracy and safeguards. It has no robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Generative AI remains subject to existing Canadian privacy laws.
Nine principles: legal authority and consent, appropriate purposes, necessity and proportionality, transparency, accountability, access, limiting collection, accuracy, safeguards.
Developers should avoid 'no-go zones' and use red-teaming to find misuse.
Developers should keep dataset documentation and carry out independent audits.
Organisations should provide a challenge mechanism and human review for significant decisions.
